style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Extreme close-up macro photograph of a disassembled carbon monoxide alarm showing its internal sensor board, resting on a textured concrete workbench in a utility closet. 100mm macro lens, shallow depth of field, one razor-sharp focal plane on the sensor component. Soft directional daylight from the left casting a long contact shadow. Extreme asymmetry with the hero object off-centre on the right thirds, background falling away. Bone white, charcoal, and brushed steel palette, visible dust and surface texture, fine film grain, muted modern editorial aesthetic, no people, no text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, UI, watermark, logos, typography
rationale: The story revolves around a specific physical component—the sensor inside a CO alarm—and its failure despite the siren working. Editorial macro focuses intimately on this device, highlighting its physical reality as a limited-life instrument rather than a permanent fixture.
subject: a disassembled carbon monoxide alarm showing its internal sensor
core_thesis: A carbon monoxide alarm is a limited-life measuring instrument whose sensor fails before its electronics do, leaving consumers with a false sense of security when recalling dangerous gas boilers.
core_conflict: Electronic longevity vs sensor decay (the test button proves the siren, not the sensor).
composition: extreme asymmetry with the hero object off-centre on the right thirds
